open_points.subject: owner sign-in
open_points.text: “Every change in the owner interface carries the CSRF protection bound to its session” and A04 requires “for the owner, a valid owner session, then its CSRF value”, but signing in creates the session and therefore can carry neither.
open_points.question: Is sign-in exempt from the owner-session and CSRF requirements, and if so, which other pre-session requests are exempt?
options: Only sign-in is exempt
Sign-in and its initial form are exempt
A temporary pre-authentication session and CSRF value are required
open_points.default_guess: Only the sign-in submission is exempt.

open_points.subject: owner session cookie
open_points.text: The cookie is “sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine” and “only to Registry's own origin”, but cookie Domain, Path, SameSite and the behavior on same-machine HTTP are not defined.
open_points.question: What exact cookie scope and attributes are required, and may a session cookie be sent over same-machine HTTP?
options: Host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure whenever HTTPS is used; permit local HTTP
Always Secure and require HTTPS everywhere
Use another explicitly declared cookie policy
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, Secure on HTTPS, while permitting the stated local-HTTP case.

open_points.subject: check ordering within stage 1
open_points.text: Stage 1 says “a valid owner session, then its CSRF value, then a confirmation value”, while the same rule says “When several checks of one stage fail, the answer names every one of them.”
open_points.question: Do owner-session, CSRF and confirmation checks short-circuit in their stated order, or are all stage-1 failures evaluated and returned together?
options: Short-circuit session, then CSRF, then confirmation
Aggregate every stage-1 failure
Short-circuit security checks but aggregate other checks in the stage
open_points.default_guess: Short-circuit the owner-session, CSRF and confirmation checks in that order.

open_points.subject: agent project-set check
open_points.text: Stage (2) assigns “the session and its set” to the agent-authority check, but stage (6) again lists “not in the set” as a lifecycle failure.
open_points.question: At which stage is project membership checked, and can any later validation run after membership fails?
options: Only stage 2, hiding every later failure
Only stage 6
Stage 2 for disclosure hiding and a second consistency check at stage 6
open_points.default_guess: Check membership only at stage 2 and stop on failure.

open_points.subject: empty audit erasure
open_points.text: R0-66 says the audit erasure “leaves an entry of its own naming the date”, while A15 says “An erasure that removes no entry changes nothing: it is accepted, writes no entry and mints no confirmation id.”
open_points.question: Does a confirmed erasure that matches no entries write an erasure audit entry and confirmation id?
options: No entry and no confirmation id
Always write an entry and mint an id
Refuse an erasure that would remove nothing
open_points.default_guess: Follow A15: accept it as a no-op with no entry or confirmation id.

open_points.subject: import file digest
open_points.text: The mapping, confirmation, migration closure and audit entry identify the file “by its digest”, but no digest algorithm, byte canonicalization or collision handling is declared.
open_points.question: How is the import file digest computed and compared, and what happens if two different uploaded byte sequences have the same digest?
options: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with a specified cryptographic algorithm and treat equality as file identity
Digest a canonical parsed representation
Store and compare both the digest and exact uploaded bytes
open_points.default_guess: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with a release-fixed cryptographic algorithm and use constant-time digest comparison.

open_points.subject: import confirmation binding
open_points.text: A13 singles out “for the import, the file's digest and the picks”, while A16 says confirmation applies “the file of that digest, the picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing else.”
open_points.question: Must the confirmation value be bound directly to names, aliases and all Customer mapping values as well as to the file digest and picks?
options: Bind every mapped input explicitly
Bind only digest and picks and reread the remaining values from session state
Bind a digest of the complete displayed mapping
open_points.default_guess: Bind a digest of the complete displayed mapping, including every name, alias and Customer value.

open_points.subject: missing configured store
open_points.text: A17 says that when “the store's configured file does not exist” Registry creates a new empty store, while R0-89 says that when the store is lost the owner restores the newest kept backup.
open_points.question: How does startup distinguish an intentional first installation from loss of an existing production store, so it does not silently serve a new empty production history?
options: An explicit initialization flag or command is required to create a store
A missing store always creates an empty store
A durable installation marker distinguishes first initialization from loss
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit initialization operation before creating a new empty store.

open_points.subject: store and backup locations
open_points.text: The store and backup location must be “different places, neither inside the other”, but the text does not define path normalization, symbolic links, bind mounts or filesystem aliases.
open_points.question: By what filesystem identity and containment rules are equality and nesting checked?
options: Compare canonical resolved paths and reject symlink aliases
Compare configured path strings only
Require separate filesystem or mount identities
open_points.default_guess: Resolve canonical paths, including symlinks, before checking equality and containment.

open_points.subject: configuration validation boundary
open_points.text: “The configuration holds exactly these items and no other” and “an unknown item fails the start”, but the text does not say what source or namespace counts as Registry configuration.
open_points.question: Which inputs are inspected for unknown items—for example, a dedicated file or prefix, command-line options, or the process's entire environment?
options: Only keys in a dedicated Registry configuration namespace
Every process environment variable
Only a fixed configuration file
open_points.default_guess: Treat only a dedicated Registry-prefixed namespace as configuration.

open_points.subject: backup encryption
open_points.text: Each backup is “encrypted with the backup key” and exposes metadata readable without the key, but the encryption construction, nonce handling, authentication and protection of the plaintext metadata are not defined.
open_points.question: What authenticated-encryption format is required, and which metadata must be cryptographically authenticated?
options: A release-fixed authenticated-encryption format authenticating all plaintext metadata
Encryption without authenticated metadata
A platform-provided encrypted container whose exact contract is declared elsewhere
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-fixed authenticated-encryption format and authenticate all plaintext metadata as associated data.

open_points.subject: daily and post-import backup scheduling
open_points.text: A18 says “Besides the run after an accepted import, at most one backup is kept per UTC day”, while catch-up runs depend on whether “no backup was made that UTC day.”
open_points.question: Does a successful post-import backup count as that day's daily backup, and does an already completed daily backup suppress or coexist with the post-import run?
options: The post-import backup is additional and never suppresses the daily run
Any successful backup satisfies the daily requirement
The post-import run is additional only when the day's scheduled backup already exists
open_points.default_guess: Keep the post-import backup as an explicit additional run, and still apply the once-per-day rule to the scheduled backup.

open_points.subject: repeating an import after pre-backup store loss
open_points.text: R0-89 requires the owner to keep “the export file and the picks, names and aliases given in the import”, but A16 also requires each new Customer's name, kind and tax-id choice to repeat the same import mapping.
open_points.question: Which complete set of import mapping inputs must the owner retain until a checked backup holds the import, including the Customer values required by A16?
options: Retain every confirmed mapping input, including Customer name, kind and tax-id choice
Retain only the fields R0-89 explicitly lists and ask for Customer values again
Derive and preserve the complete mapping separately from the listed inputs
open_points.default_guess: Retain the complete confirmed mapping, including all Customer values.
